Olga / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We have an upcoming scheduled cutover (staging -> prod) for customer tenant: Acme Retail (will be using the dedicated private VPC). Before we sign off, our NOC needs the following evidence to close the network acceptance:

- BFD session logs showing neighbor up for 10 minutes on the underlay and overlay BGP peering.
- MTU probe results (1500 vs 9000) for the p2p links and GRE/GENEVE interfaces.
- A short tcpdump/pcap capture illustrating correct DSCP preservation across the service mesh demarcation.
- The final runbook with explicit rollback steps for a binary rollback and config drift checks.

Can you provide these (pcaps + runbook) and call out any known MTU pitfalls for our colo (Equinix DC3 BR)? We're also seeing sporadic MSS clamping on the tenant NAT; if you have mitigation steps please include.

I'll attach our acceptance checklist once I have your artifacts — aim is to complete by EOD Wed (US Pacific).

Thanks,
Samir
Network Engineering
EdgeScale Systems

Subject: Re: Private VPC deploy — telemetry, MTU/BFD checks and runbook evidence

Samir —

Appreciate the clear ask. We're attaching the initial artifacts and a short checklist. High level notes up front:

- BFD: we validated session stability for 15 minutes on the staging peering (underlay: jumbo-9k enabled on the Equinix leafs we tested). BFD timers used 300/900 (min rx/tx) with 3 detection multipliers.
- MTU: our default overlay is 9000, but GRE/Geneve adds ~50 bytes; where the colo fabric enforces 1500 we fall back and enable MSS-clamp on the tenant SNAT gateway. We'll include a preflight MTU probe script.
- DSCP: service-mesh sidecars currently preserve DSCP; the demarc translation rule in the vpc-gateway makes no DSCP rewrites. The included pcap shows DSCP 46 for voice flow preserved across demarc.
- Rollback: runbook has two rollback rails: (1) immediate service-gateway BGP shutdown to failover to hosted fallback, (2) staged restore of prior config using saved-runbooks + check-sums. We also included post-rollback smoke tests.

See attached: vpc-deploy-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook + rollback), underlay-diagram.svg (annotated interfaces), pcap-samples.zip (pcaps + trace notes). Also linking a short iperf/MTU probe we ran.

Next steps: can your NOC confirm the exact leaf interface names on your side so we can match counters? If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min packet walk-through next week.

- Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts — we've started ingesting the PCAPs. A couple of quick clarifications before we mark acceptance:

1) Your BFD logs show neighbor flaps at 11:03 UTC (short 2s dip) — can you confirm whether that coincides with the staging control-plane maintenance window? If it was a test, we just need an annotated log.

2) The MTU probe report shows mixed results on two of three p2p legs to Equinix BR-DC3 (one path had PMTU blackhole behavior at 1460). Do you have the explicit MSS-clamp value you applied to tenant-SNAT? Please supply the exact iptables/tc rule we should expect to see.

3) For the rollback flow, will your runbook auto-detect config drift or is that manual? We prefer an automated diff against the golden config (sha256) as part of the acceptance evidence.

If you can reply with the two small items (annotated BFD log + exact iptables example + note on automated diff), we'll proceed to sign off and inject the deployment window on our calendar.

Nina Ortiz
EdgeScale NOC
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: EdgeScale NOC <noc@edgescale.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@edgescale.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deploy — telemetry, MTU/BFD checks and runbook evidence

Nina —

Quick answers inline:

1) BFD dip at 11:03 UTC: that was an intentional test from our side (staging flapping exercise). I've attached an annotated-bfd-log.txt inside the pcap archive; we flagged it and the runbook notes it as expected behavior during the controlled test window.

2) MSS clamp: we use iptables rule at the tenant SNAT gateway to clamp MSS to 1400 for connections that hit the 1500-only underlay. Example (copied from runbook, verbatim):

iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400

We also add a tc qdisc mirror rule for egress to ensure PMTU discovery isn't silently dropped (details in runbook, section 4.2).

3) Drift detection: runbook includes an automated golden-config diff (sha256) step executed by our deployment agent prior to cutover. The agent will fail the deployment if checksums differ; manual override requires two approvers (SRE lead + Solutions Eng). Artifact: golden-configs/sha256.txt included in the Drive link.

I'll follow up with a short 30-min packet-walk if you want to go through the pcap together. If not, please confirm and we'll request the cutover window formally (we'll push a canary cut to 2% tenant traffic first).

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
